There's one particular image of my mother that haunts me still and I haven't really talked about it, but I think it's the moment she finally realised it was the end for her. She'd had lung cancer and it had spread to her brain and she'd all of a sudden gone downhill pretty quickly, to the point where she wasn't making sense and stuff and didn't really understand what was going on.

She got taken into hospital because of a leg infection of all things (horsefly bites used to send her there all the time even before she was ill), and she's laying there in the hospital bed, her eye sight had started to go too because of the tumour on her brain, and she's talking to me. "When I get out of here we need to go and see the optician because my eyes are bad" \- she didn't say it as eloquently as that, her speech is slurred and she's struggling to find the right words. 

All of a sudden she turns to look at me and grabs my hand, and she just stares at me for a good 30 seconds and squeezes my hand tighter. It's in that moment I feel like everything came into place in her head and she could think properly and she just understood that she wasn't getting out of hospital again. 

So yeah, having to sit through things like this, you're honestly sometimes not sure whether or not your loved one would have just been knocked over one day. There's no right way to have someone die who is a part of your life and I don't know which i'd have preferred.
